title: Building the Agent Image
description: A minimal Dockerfile that installs the tools an agent needs, adds opencode and a second agent, points at the host model, and drops to an ordinary user.

steps.description: This is `Dockerfile.agent`, the minimal standalone container. `FROM node:24-bookworm-slim` starts from a small Node image, and a container is what replaces the permission prompt, since it bounds what the agent can reach at all.

The first `RUN` installs the tools the agent needs: `git` so it can commit its own work, `ripgrep` because agents reach for it, `ca-certificates` so HTTPS works, and `curl` for the omp installer. The package lists are removed after.
`npm install -g opencode-ai` installs opencode into the image. The next `RUN` installs Oh My Pi, a second agent, from `https://omp.sh/install`, placing its binary in `/usr/local/bin`.

`ENV OLLAMA_HOST=http://host.docker.internal:11434` points at the host, because the model lives on the host, not in the container, and code inside reaches it across the container wall at this address.

The container creates a non-root user `agent` and switches to it, so anything that goes wrong goes wrong as an ordinary user. `WORKDIR /workspace` sets the working directory, and `CMD ["opencode"]` is the default command.

steps.question: The page says notice what is not in the image: no API key, no token, no ~/.ssh, and no what?
